clue.text: University degree — so simple

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a first university degree
sic is Latin for 'so, thus', used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a university degree is a rather simple thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is elementary and plain, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Lawyer is abrupt in manner

explanation.surface: A lawyer is described as curt with clients.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is informally called a brief, and a brief reply is a short, curt one.

clue.text: Feeling angry and unusually energised

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the next word are to be put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone feels cross and unusually full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the nine letters of ENERGISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming furious.

clue.text: Rock musician not standing up after applause

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the applause

parts.note: a clap is a burst of applause

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word not is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A rock star stays seated even after the applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns NOT into TON in this down clue; Eric Clapton is the guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton is a famous rock guitarist, an example of a rock musician.

clue.text: Imitate traveller's tale about wild animal

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

indicators.note: about means the tale goes round the animal

parts.note: a lie is a made-up tale
the wildcat is a wild animal, here just cat

explanation.surface: Someone copies a commercial traveller's story about a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. A 'traveller' in crosswords is often a sales representative on the road, and the wildcat lets 'wild animal' stand for the domestic word.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to copy or reproduce exactly, a synonym of imitate.

clue.text: Long-tailed creature making you react oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks out the odd-numbered letters of the word react

explanation.surface: Seeing a long-tailed animal makes a person jump in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of 'react'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a rodent with a long, bare tail.

clue.text: Indicating aspect of builder's work's old-fashioned

parts.note: pointing is a builder's job of filling the mortar joints in brickwork
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: A remark that some part of a builder's craft has gone out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 's of 'work's' stands for 'is' and is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing out is a phrasal verb for showing or drawing attention, a synonym of indicating.

clue.text: Forthcoming shopping expedition here?

explanation.surface: A shopping trip is coming soon, and a question asks where it will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: What is coming up is said to be lying ahead, and a shopping trip takes place inside a shop.

clue.text: Choose to perform in a small part

indicators.note: in places the verb inside the article and abbreviation

parts.note: PT is the short form of part
to do something is to carry it out or perform it

explanation.surface: An actor agrees to take a small role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DO inside A and PT; 'small' signals the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a plan or option is to take it up, a synonym of choose.

clue.text: Alteration to house gives former partner stress

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
tension is mental strain or stress

explanation.surface: Building work on a home leaves someone's former partner under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an added room or wing built onto a home.

clue.text: I subsequently receive account that's inaccurate

indicators.note: receive means the word for afterwards takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: next means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: Someone admits an account they later receive was not accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receive' signals the container; 'subsequently' means afterwards, coming in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise or not correct, a synonym of inaccurate.

clue.text: Briefly popular member of Blair's first cabinet

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Clare Short was International Development Secretary in Tony Blair's 1997 cabinet

explanation.surface: A quick note on someone who was popular in Tony Blair's first government.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a UK Labour minister who served under Tony Blair from 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: In short is an idiom meaning to put it concisely, the sense of briefly.

clue.text: As punishment, cheat gets a sort of carpeting

parts.note: a fine is a monetary punishment
to twist is slang for to swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A cheat's penalty is to be given a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like a telling-off, the punishment of the surface; here it is literal floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine twist is a type of carpet with tightly twisted pile yarn, an example of floor covering.

clue.text: During time at school, one doesn't want son to mix with others

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a term is one of the periods of the school year

indicators.note: doesn't want means the letter for son is dropped

parts.note: a single is one person, an unattached one
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A pupil during term doesn't want her son mixing with other children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't want' removes S from SINGLE to leave INGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermingle is to blend or mingle together with others.

clue.text: Report, one implicating infamous playwright

indicators.note: implicating means the clue words fold the name within them

explanation.surface: A report in which one person implicates a notorious dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implicating' points to the letters spanning 'Report, one'; Joe Orton was a scandalous 1960s English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton was a notorious English dramatist known for shocking black comedies.

clue.text: Brief moment in power, say

indicators.note: in places the shortened moment inside the word for power

parts.note: force is power or strength

indicators.note: brief means the word for a moment is cut short at its end

parts.note: an instant is a moment

explanation.surface: A short time spent in authority, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts the last letter from the word for a moment, giving INSTAN, and 'in' signals the container; 'say' introduces an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an example, as is the phrase for example.

clue.text: Kiss a chef stirring food for snack

indicators.note: stirring suggests the letters are mixed up like ingredients in a pot

explanation.surface: Someone kisses a cook who is stirring up some snack food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' rearranges the letters of 'Kiss a chef'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishcakes are fried patties of fish and potato often eaten as a light meal.

clue.text: Runner, extremely sleek one

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the extremes, first and last, of the word sleek

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A racer who is very streamlined is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'sleek'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long runner on which you glide over snow, like a sledge runner.

clue.text: Holier-than-thou Israeli convert clutches part of bible

indicators.note: clutches means the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation inside
convert means the letters of Israeli are changed into a new form

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A self-righteous Israeli convert grips a portion of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' rearranges the seven letters and 'clutches' signals the container, giving SAI-NT-LIER around the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Holier-than-thou is comparative in form, and saintlier means more virtuous or pious.

clue.text: Sorrowful and dejected, principally

indicators.note: principally picks the principal, leading letters of the clue words

explanation.surface: Someone is above all unhappy and downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the first three words spell the answer, which also describes the mood they name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad means unhappy, a synonym of both sorrowful and dejected.

clue.text: Company given speech by NCO

parts.note: Corp is short for corporal, a non-commissioned officer
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A firm receives a talk from a sergeant-type officer.
explanation.walkthrough: An NCO is a non-commissioned officer in the army, such as a corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation is a large business firm, a synonym of company.

clue.text: Famous chef's bag: pigeon?

explanation.surface: A celebrity cook's handbag is asked whether it is a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Carrier was a celebrity cook on British television in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Carrier was a TV cook, a bag for shopping and a homing bird both take the same word.

clue.text: Broadcaster has taped Dean Martin number ones for fan

indicators.note: has taped means the broadcaster holds the initials within, as a recording is held

parts.note: an airer is one who airs, or broadcasts, programmes

indicators.note: number ones means the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A radio station records Dean Martin's chart-toppers for a listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number ones' takes D and M; 'has taped' puts them inside AIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a devotee or supporter, a synonym of fan.

clue.text: Confronted by bully … um … cringe

indicators.note: Confronted by places the hesitation behind the word for bully

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or bully them
er is a hesitation noise like um

explanation.surface: Faced with a thug, someone stammers and shrinks back.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink back in fear, a synonym of cringe.

clue.text: Jam said to make you healthy

indicators.note: said means the word for jam is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a hole is a difficult situation, as is a jam

explanation.surface: Someone claims that eating jam is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like the preserve; it means a fix or tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole in an older sense means sound and well, in good health.

clue.text: Hints from very close friends

explanation.surface: Clues are given by people who are dear to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest indirectly, and intimates as a noun means one's closest companions.

clue.text: Irishman died, captured in battle

indicators.note: captured means the name holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogy

explanation.surface: An Irish soldier died after being taken prisoner in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' puts D inside SEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan was the 1870 Franco-Prussian War battle where Napoleon III was taken prisoner.

clue.text: Fly today with Monarch as carrier

indicators.note: as carrier means the monarch carries the word for today within it

parts.note: a king is a monarch
now means at the present time, today

explanation.surface: Someone flies now with the airline Monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Monarch was a British airline, so 'Fly' and 'carrier' suggest air travel; 'Fly' means shrewd.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is British slang for sharp or shrewd, and knowing means worldly-wise and astute.

clue.text: Anxious wife I order about

indicators.note: about means the following letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous wife gives orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of 'I order'.
explanation.definitionFit: Worried means troubled and uneasy, a synonym of anxious.

clue.text: Be well acquainted with Western Isles

explanation.surface: Someone claims to know the Hebrides well.
explanation.definitionFit: Wis is an archaic verb for to know, and WIS is the short form for the Hebridean islands off Scotland.

clue.text: Female bird perches on vessel in port

indicators.note: perches on means the bird sits before the vessel in this across clue

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
the erne is the sea eagle
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: A hen bird settles on a ship docked in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is a port town in Kent, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is a harbour town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent.

clue.text: About time crewmen raced again

indicators.note: About means the sailors go around the period

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors or crewmen
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A ship's crew raced once more at around the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' signals the container; Royal Navy sailors are the crewmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reran means ran a race a second time.
